title: Practice: a cost model and a model router, graded on a cost table (TypeScript)

cases.id: m1 cost of a plain request and the cheapest model that meets the tier
cases.says: A plain request is priced from input and output, and the router returns the cheapest model at or above the tier

cases.id: e1 cache reads and writes are priced by their own multipliers
cases.says: Cache writes cost 1.25 and 2 times input, reads use the model's own multiplier, and an unsplit write is the 5-minute kind

cases.id: e2 the batch discount halves every part of the cost
cases.says: The batch discount halves every part of the cost, cache parts included

cases.id: e3 the router picks by cost and tier not by the order of the catalog
cases.says: The router picks by cost and tier, whatever the order of the catalog

cases.id: e4 a model whose context or output limit is too small is skipped
cases.says: A model with too small a context window or output limit is skipped

cases.id: e5 deprecated models are skipped and an empty choice raises
cases.says: Deprecated models are skipped, and a choice with no model raises NoModelError

cases.id: e6 a tie goes to the lower tier
cases.says: A cost tie goes to the lower tier
